column1: Proposed scope: front-facing live overlays, one person, shirt photos and three preset hairstyles.
Team review needed: browser/native platform, supported movement, test phones, targets and estimates.
Lower priorities are candidates across four sprints. Keep Sprint No. blank for this submission.

column2: Description
Make the app easy to use on a smartphone.
Build the app without using paid APIs.
Ask for camera access and help users if permission is denied.
Show a live view from the front camera.
Turn off the camera when the user leaves the preview.
Keep live video on the phone without uploading or saving it.
Let users choose between trying on shirts and hairstyles.
Detect the user’s upper body in the camera.
Show a sample shirt on the user.
Keep the shirt lined up as the user moves while facing the camera.
Hide the shirt when body tracking is lost and bring it back when tracking returns.
Let users take or retake a picture of a shirt.
Let users upload a picture of a shirt from their phone.
Show an error if an uploaded picture cannot be used.
Give users basic tips for taking a clear shirt picture.
Let users crop and rotate their shirt pictures.
Let users trace around a shirt to remove its background.
Let users mark key points on the shirt to help line it up.
Let users try on the shirt from their own picture.
Let users adjust the shirt’s size and position or reset it.
Detect the user’s face and head position.
Include at least three hairstyle options that the team can use.
Show the selected hairstyle on the user’s head.
Keep the hairstyle lined up as the user moves their head.
Hide the hairstyle when face tracking is lost and bring it back when tracking returns.
Let users switch hairstyles during the live preview.
Let users adjust the hairstyle’s size and position or reset it.
Guide users on where to stand and how to face the camera.
Reduce shaking and jumping in the shirt and hairstyle previews.
Keep the live preview running smoothly on the phones used for testing.
Show when the tracking tools are loading and let users retry if loading fails.
Keep shirts and hairstyles lined up in the mirrored camera view.
Make the app work when the phone is held upright or sideways.
Explain that the app shows appearance, not clothing sizes or fit.
Explain how the app uses the camera and handles saved pictures.
Let users take a picture of their current preview.
Let users save preview pictures to their phone.
Let users save shirts in the app and try them on again later.
Let users delete saved shirts or clear all saved pictures.
Make the main features work on the iPhone and Android phones used for testing.
Automatically remove a shirt picture’s background and allow manual fixes.
Keep the user’s hands and arms visible in front of the virtual shirt.
